explanation: Deconcentration involves the passing down of selected administrative functions to lower levels or units within government agencies or departments with the centre remaining in control Like the series of political office arrangements and portfolios in the Hausa/Fulani Empire i.e the Galadima, Waziri and the rest, deconcentration of power is obtainable unlike in devolution which Options B and D implicitly cover. Option A refers to the Decentralization of powers.

question: Which of the following was not responsible for the coalition between A. G and N. C. N. C.?

options.text: Awolowo's faction seeking to get N. P. C. out of power as opposed to Akintola's option
contest for the federal election of 1964
Akintola's faction which broke out of A. G. to form UPP

explanation: All the following options facilitated the coalition of the action Group and the National Council of the Nigerian Citizens except the The Kano Riot of 1953

question: The Hausa/Fulani Empire as a result of its heterogeneous population adopted_________

options.text: A unitary system where full concentration of power prevailed
A federal structure where powers were decentralized although autocratic
A quasi federal structure with devolution
A partial federal set up with deconcentration

explanation: The hausa/fulani empire for geo-political reasons apportioned different portfolios of authorities for serve the multiplicity of functions and administrative interests. The offices of Sarkin fada, as head of palace workers, Waziri as prime minister among others are pointers in this regard.

question: The most recent target plans and agenda of the United Nations are known as the______
explanation: The 17 United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) are the most recent aspirational global agenda for the sake of environmental sustainability, strong governance institutions and partnerships among related others.

question: The fact that the office of the Chairman is rotational in ECOWAS makes it a perfect example of a/an ........
explanation: A collegiate system refers to a system where leadership is shared or rotated among members rather than being permanently held by one entity. In ECOWAS (Economic Community of West African States), the Chairmanship is rotational among member states, meaning no single country or leader permanently dominates the organization. This makes ECOWAS a collegiate body, where power is collectively exercised and shared.

question: The political party serves as________

options.text: A platform upon which the rights and liberties of the people can be attained
The group aggregating the interest of all in the state
A platform for rebelling against military rule

explanation: A political party primarily serves as a platform for interest representation by: Organizing and representing the views and interests of different groups in society. Competing for political power through elections. Influencing government policies in favor of their supporters.

question: Under the 1999 constitution, the Chief Law Officer and the Supreme Court Judge respectively are the_______

options.text: Chief Registrar of the Supreme Court, Chief Justice

explanation: The Attorney General of the Federation is the same as the Minister of Justice while the judge at the Supreme Court level is the Chief Justice.s

question: Implementations of the target programmes of the government is the primary duty of the _____ a part of the _____
explanation: The Civil Service is an integral branch of the public service which primarily functions to implement the policies of the government.

question: Twelve States creation is a known achievement of the ... Regime
explanation: Yakubu Gowon created 12 states for Nigeria in 1967.

question: The Green Revolution programme was the effected manifesto of the ........ in 1979
explanation: The National Party of Nigeria (NPN) is popularly known for its Green Revolution agricultural project in the late 1979s.

question: A vote of no confidence means______

options.text: the same as impeachment in a presidential system
the ability of the head of state to dissolve the parliament when collective responsibility fails to hold
the act of showing disapproval to the prime minister having breached the collective responsibility doctrine
the disapproval with dismissal in effect, the ministers and its head

explanation: A vote of no confidence is a formal motion passed by the legislature (parliament) to indicate that the government (headed by the Prime Minister) no longer has the support of the majority. When passed: The Prime Minister and the entire cabinet must resign. It usually leads to the formation of a new government or a call for fresh elections.

question: One of the following reasons is unlikely to necessitate the emergence of a federal system?
explanation: Other options are necessary reasons for the adoption of a federal system except for sake of defining or strengthening the political sovereignty which invariably belongs to the citizens.

question: Generally, a political party with only manifestoes without fulfilment is a/an _____
explanation: Elitist is often used as a critique label, to describe a political party definitive of social class and rankings of top profiled politicians without much agenda for social justice. Elitist parties are often seen as focusing more on presenting themselves as representatives of a particular elite or ideology rather than actively implementing their policies or fulfilling their promises.

question: The federal judge under the 1963 constitution could be removed by the______
explanation: 2/3 majority support or vote of the National Assembly members was enough under the 1963 Constitution to remove a federal judge.

question: A form of government organized by a council of military officers is called______
explanation: A stratocracy is a form of government headed by military chiefs.

question: In most recent times, a seemingly workable solution to the Nigerian federal question is that of_______
explanation: Although Options A, B and C are recurring options for the Nigerian federalism, the clarion call for restructuring is louder than ever before.

question: Lobbying is often a strategy adopted by________
explanation: Pressure groups often adopt lobbying as a negotiation mechanism with critical governement stakeholders and or legislators so that significant policies and laws giving effect to their interests are implemented.

question: A party can be said to have national outlook if________

options.text: it is ethnic based but has branches all over the state
its membership cut across ethnic boundaries
it is registered by the electoral commission as a national party
it is headed by individuals who are famous within and without the country

explanation: A political party has a national outlook when it represents diverse ethnic, religious, and regional groups rather than being limited to a specific ethnic or regional interest.

question: Argumentation, negotiation and deliberation on the subject matter of a bill begins at the_______
explanation: The second reading is where debate, argumentation, negotiation, and deliberation on the subject matter of a bill begin. At this stage: Lawmakers discuss the general principles of the bill. They debate its merits and implications before deciding whether it should progress to the next stage. If the bill passes the second reading, it moves to the committee stage for detailed examination.

question: An order compelling a lower court or public corporation to perform in accordance with legitimacy is called_________
explanation: Writ (i.e Order) of Mandamus is usually issued to mandate a public authority to perform its statutory or the functions tied to its establishment. On the alternative, the great writ means the habeas corpus writ issued to order the release of a body or person unlawfully detained or imprisoned to stand judgement

question: The newspaper established by Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe to project the interest of nationalists was__________
explanation: The West African Pilot was the newspaper of Dr Azikiwe which served as a medium for propagating nationalist ideas and solidarity movements towards self-realization.

question: According to Lewis Samuel, '________ is identified with pure conquest and unequivocal exploitation...'
explanation: The ideology of regressive imperialism is pure economic advantage and enrichment of the imperialists devoid of any ethical consideration.s

question: The term ultra vires means_________

options.text: the exercise of supervisory functions by the judiciary
a situation where a public authority dutifully performs its functions
a situation where a public authority acts beyond the scope of its duties
the act of exercising administrative competence over a matter

explanation: A public authority is said to have ultra vires when it has acted beyond the boundaries of its duties as provided for in its enabling law or as prescribed by the Executive.

question: The right of a citizen to seek redress means the right to________

options.text: seek an appeal under another judgement

explanation: Seek an appeal under another judgement is the best answer because, ''the right to seek redress'' is a fundamental element of rule of law. It means that aggrieved parties should be afforded the opportunity to have their cases re-examined especially by a court of higher authority.

question: The Brussel conference in 1889/90 was based on______

options.text: putting an end to slave trade
furthering the decision on colonialism as previously discussed in the Berlin conference
deciding on how to penetrate Africa for economic adventurism

explanation: The Brussel Conference unlike the Berlin Conference was targeted at the reconsideration of the unjust virtues and vices occasioned by colonialism, thereby specifically seeking to eradicate slave trade and related activities.

question: The area from which one or more members or representatives are elected in public offices is called the electoral ........
explanation: Constituency is the definition for the political area from which an individual is elected into a representative office.

question: ____ is noted for having said "man by nature is a political animal"
explanation: According to Aristotle, every human interaction intersects with political determinations and interests.

question: In the all-Nigerian constitutional conference of 1950_______

options.text: all official members of the legislative council participated
it was resolved that the Nigerians federation be organized on ethnic basis
it was concluded that a quasi-federal structure should be developed for colonial Nigeria
all unofficial members of the legislative council participated

explanation: Recognizing and acknowledging the relative importance of direct participation and contribution by people in their own affairs, the All-Nigerian Constitutional Conference marked an unprecendented attendance of all previously relegated unofficial members of the local legislature.

question: A predominant feature of the Precolonial governance system was that_________

options.text: the British Indirect rule system penetrated it largely
the governance structures were largely undefined

explanation: Throughout the precolonial era in Nigeria, the native laws of the people governed them. They were largely unwritten and enforced by distinct units set in place for those purposes.

question: Nigeria's federalism is often considered a flaw along the standard test of the Classical federalism ideology labelled along with_______
explanation: Kenneth Clinton Wheare is noted to having postulated that the fundamental, negotiable element of federalism is voluntary submission of rights by the component units in a federal set up.

question: Class stratification is a peculiar feature of___________
explanation: In a capitalist system, there is a clear differentiation gap between the ruling class and the ruled or the proletarates.

question: That type of sovereignty that thrives on legitimacy is__________

options.text: vested on any form of government

explanation: Legal sovereignty expresses his will in legal terms. This means it can only declare according to law the will of the state.

question: The most representative organ of the united nations is the_______
explanation: General Assembly. The UN General Assembly comprises the Heads of State and Government of all the State Parties in the UN body.

question: A set of internalized norms which guides political action is called ________
explanation: Laws are formal rules established by a governing authority that are expected to be followed by members of society. They guide behaviour and political action by providing a framework for acceptable conduct and legal processes.

question: A condition for judicial independence is the appointment of judges by the __________
explanation: An independent judiciary is one which is free from the interference of the other two arms of government, the executive and legislative. A condition for judicial independence is the appointment of judges by the Judicial Service Commission. The Judicial Service Commission is responsible for the appointment, promotion and discipline of judges. This system helps ensure that the judiciary remains independent from the executive and legislative branches.

question: Within the United Nations, the vote power is exercised in __________
explanation: Within the United Nations, voting power is exercised in the Security Council. The Security Council is responsible for maintaining international peace and security, and its decisions require the affirmative votes of at least nine of its fifteen members, including the concurring votes of all five permanent members (the United States, the United Kingdom, France, Russia, and China) to pass certain resolutions.

question: Southern Nigeria was divided into Eastern and Western provinces for administrative purposes in _________
explanation: In 1939, Southern Nigeria was officially divided into the Eastern and Western Provinces by Governor Bernard Bourdillon for administrative convenience. Before this, Southern Nigeria was administered as a single entity after the 1914 amalgamation of the Northern and Southern Protectorates. The division allowed for better governance and set the foundation for the later creation of Nigeria’s regions in 1954.

question: A feature unique to General Murtala Muhammed's Supreme Military Council as compared to that of General Yakubu Gowon was the _________

options.text: inclusion of the civilians as members
exclusion of military governors from the council
inclusion of the chief justice as a member
the exclusion of the Inspector General of police from the council

explanation: A feature unique to General Murtala Muhammed's Supreme Military Council, compared to that of General Yakubu Gowon, was the exclusion of military governors from the council. General Murtala Muhammed's regime, which came to power in 1975, restructured the Supreme Military Council (SMC) to exclude military governors from its membership. New appointed military governors were not given seats on the supreme military council, but instead were expected to administer federal policies handed by Murtala Muhammed.

question: Which of the following is not associated with local government elections?
explanation: In local government elections, terms like ballot box, electoral officer, and ward are directly relevant, as they are involved in the voting process and the organisation of local elections. A constituency is more commonly associated with national or larger-scale legislative elections.

question: A system of government in which power derives from total control of the instruments of force is called ___________
explanation: Facism is a form of government headed by a dictator, in which government has a total control over all activities in the state.

question: The economic basis of feudalism is __________
explanation: Feudalism was a system that primarily relied on agriculture as its economic foundation, with the majority of the population engaged in farming to support their livelihoods and those of their lords.

question: NEPAD was adopted during the OAU summit held in _________
explanation: NEPAD was adopted in the 37th OAU Summit in Lusaka, Zambia in July 2001

question: In a democracy, sovereignty is in _________
explanation: Democracy is concentrated on the people, the people's ability to exercise power directly or through a representative.

question: The highest court in Nigeria before 1963 was the _________

options.text: Judicial Committees of the Privy Council

explanation: Judicial Committee of Privy Council is the highest court of appeal for British Territories established on 13th, August 1833. The Privy Council served as the final court of appeal for Nigeria during the colonial period and up until the Nigerian Constitution of 1963, when Nigeria established its own Supreme Court as the highest judicial authority in the country.

question: Rates are generally collected in Nigeria by ________
explanation: Local government generates revenue through the collection of rates on radio and television, market shops, motor parks etc

question: Warrant Chiefs were appointed to __________
explanation: Colonial authorities selected some people whom they made chiefs and were given certificate of recognition. They were referred to as warrant chief who took charge of local administration

question: Which of the following is a good example of a confederal state?
explanation: In a confederal system, member states retain most of the power and delegate limited authority to the central governing body. ECOWAS is a regional organization where member countries cooperate on economic and political issues but maintain their sovereignty and control over most of their affairs. Switzerland and the USA are examples of federal states, where the central government has significant authority and shares power with regional governments. Nigeria is also a federal state with a similar structure to the USA and Switzerland.

question: The Gulf War of 1990 is an indication that the U. N. O. is unable to _______
explanation: The Gulf War of 1990 (also known as the First Gulf War) was a conflict where a U.S.-led coalition, backed by the United Nations (U.N.), fought against Iraq after it invaded Kuwait. Despite the U.N.'s efforts to maintain peace, war still broke out, proving that the U.N. cannot ensure permanent world peace.

question: The idea of making the civil service permanent, neutral and anonymous is to _________

options.text: make civil servants a functional elite

explanation: The idea of making the civil service permanent, neutral, and anonymous is to enhance efficiency in administration. Making the civil service permanent, neutral, and anonymous ensures that civil servants can perform their duties without political interference and this provides continuity and stability in administration which enhances overall efficiency.

question: Which of the following was the last to win independence from colonial rule ?
explanation: Angola was the last among the options to gain independence from colonial rule. Côte d'Ivoire – Gained independence from France in 1960. Algeria – Gained independence from France in 1962 after a long and bloody war. Tanzania – (Formerly Tanganyika) Gained independence from Britain in 1961, later uniting with Zanzibar in 1964. Angola – Gained independence from Portugal in 1975, making it the last among these options.

question: Nigeria's non-aligned policy means that she will _________

options.text: have nothing to do with the superpowers
not take sides in international issues based on ideological considerations
avoid having any dealing with any country with ideological learnings
relate only with member countries of the Non-Aligned movement

explanation: Nigeria's non-aligned policy means that she will not take sides in international issues based on ideological considerations. This policy is part of the broader Non-Aligned Movement (NAM), which emerged during the Cold War era. Nigeria, like other non-aligned countries, seeks to maintain independence and neutrality by not committing to any of the major ideological blocs (capitalism or communism). This allows for more flexibility in foreign policy and international relations.

question: Fascism developed in________
explanation: Fascism was developed in Italy under Benito Mussolini

question: A government in which control of ultimate power is by a few who rule in their selfish interest is classified as _________
explanation: An oligarchy is a form of government that places power in the hands of a few people.s

question: A characteristic feature of communism is __________
explanation: Communism often involves a centralised government with significant control over economic and political life, which can manifest as a dictatorship or a single-party state. This centralisation is meant to enforce collective ownership and eliminate class distinctions, but it frequently results in a concentration of power and limited political freedoms.

question: The Premier of Western Region immediately after independence was _________
explanation: The Premier of Western Region immediately after independence was S.L. Akintola. He became the Premier 1960, however, there was a crisis between Akinotla and Awolowo , Moses Majekodunmi was then appointed as a Sole administrator until 1963 Akintola resumed as the Premier of Western Region

question: The theory of separation of powers was first time clearly formulated by __________
explanation: The theory of separation of powers was first clearly formulated by Baron de Montesquieu in his book The Spirit of the Laws (1748). Montesquieu argued that government power should be divided among three branches—the legislative, executive, and judiciary—to prevent abuse of power. This theory influenced modern democratic governance, particularly the U.S. Constitution and many other constitutional governments worldwide.

question: The simple plurality electoral system is often criticized because _________

options.text: the ruling party may lose the election
the winner may not poll an absolute majority
it works against all opposition parties

explanation: The simple plurality electoral system, often referred to as "first-past-the-post," is criticised for several reasons, particularly for its susceptibility to manipulation.

question: When a state is subject to no other authority, it is said to be _________
explanation: Sovereignty refers to the supreme authority of a state to govern itself without interference from external powers. A sovereign state has full control over its territory and domestic and foreign policies.

question: In the First Republic, Nigeria was very reluctant to have meaningful interaction with ________
explanation: During Nigeria’s First Republic (1963–1966), the country followed a pro-Western foreign policy, maintaining close ties with Western nations like the United States, the United Kingdom, and other Commonwealth countries. Nigeria was reluctant to engage meaningfully with the Soviet Union due to the Cold War tensions and fear of communist influence in Africa. The government, led by Prime Minister Sir Abubakar Tafawa Balewa, aligned more with capitalist democracies rather than the socialist bloc.

question: The founder of the Universal Negro Improvement Association was ________
explanation: Marcus Garvey is the founder and first President-General of the Universal Negro Improvement Association and African Communities League, commonly known as UNIA. He established it with the aim of promoting the unity and self-reliance of people of African descent and advocating for the advancement of black people worldwide.

question: The Fundamental Objectives and Directive Principles of State Policy in the 1979 constitution do not include _________

options.text: concentration of wealth and provision of maximum welfare

explanation: The Fundamental Objectives and Directive Principles of State Policy in the 1979 Nigerian Constitution were designed to guide government policies and promote national development. These principles focused on democracy, social justice, federal character, national integration, and equal opportunities for all citizens. The constitution aimed to reduce the concentration of wealth in the hands of a few and instead promote fair distribution of resources and social welfare. Option C is incorrect because "concentration of wealth" contradicts the principles of the constitution.

question: In the traditional Hausa-Fulani political system, political authority was vested in the ___________
explanation: The Caliphate was divided into emirates and each headed by an emir. The Emir was the traditional ruler and held significant political, judicial, and religious authority within the emirate. The Emirate Council, composed of various officials and advisors, assisted the Emir in governance, but the ultimate authority resided with the Emir.

question: A constitution is a legal document _________

options.text: forming the basis upon which a government rules the country
only likely to succeed in countries where there is union government

explanation: A constitution is defined as a body of agreed rules and principles stating how the powers of governing a country are given and how these powers are to be exercised.

question: A meeting of the legislature is usually brought to an end with __________
explanation: A meeting of the legislature is typically brought to an end through adjournment, which means the session is temporarily suspended and will resume at a later date. Here’s what the other options mean: Prorogation – This is the formal ending of a parliamentary session by the head of state (e.g., the president or monarch), after which a new session will begin. Dissolution – This permanently ends the current parliament, usually leading to new elections. Suspension – This refers to a temporary stoppage of legislative activities, often due to disciplinary actions or special circumstances.

question: The judicial organ of government is the body which _________
explanation: The judicial organ of government performs various functions which include; punishment of offenders, settlement of disputes, safeguarding rights, protection of constitution etc. However, in summary, it is the body that interprets the law of the state.

question: A bill that applies to the whole population and is intended to promote the general welfare is called _________
explanation: Public bills are proposed laws that affect the general public and are intended to address broad issues or policy areas, rather than being tailored to specific individuals or organizations.

question: While pressure groups aim at influencing government decisions, the primary aim of political parties is to ______

options.text: promote the welfare of their members
influence legislation in order to benefit their members

explanation: A political party is defined as an organized group of citizens, who act together as a political unit, who act together as a political unit, having distinctive aims and objectives involving political questions in the state and acting together and seeking to obtain control of government

question: The charter of the United Nations was drawn up in ________
explanation: The charter of the United Nations was signed on 26th June 1945 in San Francisco

question: Which of the following was not established by the 1979 Nigerian constitution?
explanation: The National Universities Commission (NUC) was established earlier, in 1962, by the Federal Government of Nigeria to oversee the development of higher education in the country. The 1979 Constitution of Nigeria established the Police Service Commission, the Federal Electoral Commission (now known as the Independent National Electoral Commission or INEC), and the National Population Commission.

question: The delineation of constituencies is a major duty of the __________
explanation: The Electoral Commission is a body charged with organising and conducting all elections in the country. The electoral commission is also typically responsible for defining and adjusting the boundaries of electoral constituencies to ensure fair and effective representation.

question: Africans were first elected to the legislative council in British West Africa in _________
explanation: In 1923, Nigerians were first elected to the legislative council in British West Africa.

question: The application of the rule of law may be constrained by ________

options.text: securing the tenure of office of judges
employing men of proven integrity as judges

explanation: The rule of law can be constrained by invoking emergency powers. For instance, if there is a war, a state of emergency could be declared. Bad leaders may be enthroned and citizens may be denied of some of their rights.

question: The British Government revoked the charter of the Royal Niger Company and took over the direct administration of Nigeria in _________
explanation: On 1 January 1900, the Royal Niger Company transferred its territories to the British Government. This change marked the beginning of direct British colonial rule over Nigeria, transitioning from the earlier system of indirect control through the Royal Niger Company.

question: Financial allocation to local governments by the federal or the state government to supplement the cost of a project is called_____
explanation: A matching grant is a financial contribution provided by a higher level of government (federal or state) to local governments to help cover the costs of specific projects. The key aspect of a matching grant is that it requires the local government to contribute a certain amount of their own funds to receive the grant. This is done to ensure that the local government is also invested in the project and to encourage efficient use of resources. - Revenue allocation refers to the distribution of revenue (usually taxes) collected by the government among various levels of government or different sectors. - Reimbursement is the repayment of funds spent by an individual or organisation, typically for expenses already incurred. - Statutory Allocation involves the mandatory distribution of funds based on laws or regulations, often involving pre-determined formulas or criteria.

question: One of the duties of the legislature is to_______
explanation: The legislature has several key functions in a government, including exercising oversight. This involves monitoring and evaluating the actions and policies of the executive branch to ensure accountability and transparency. The legislature holds hearings, conducts investigations and reviews the implementation of laws and policies to prevent misuse of power and corruption.

question: The citizenship of a country could be acquired through______
explanation: Citizenship of a country can be acquired through different means, but the most common and legally recognized ways are birth and naturalization. Breakdown of the Two Forms of Citizenship Acquisition: By Birth – A person is automatically a citizen if they are born within the country or if one or both parents are citizens, depending on the country's laws. By Naturalization – This is a process where a foreigner applies for and is granted citizenship after meeting specific legal requirements, such as residing in the country for a specified number of years and demonstrating loyalty to the nation.

question: ____________was the method used by the British to facilitate the administration of Southern Nigeria.
explanation: Divide and rule policy, or divide and conquer, is gaining and maintaining power by breaking up larger concentrations of power into pieces that individually have less power than the one implementing the strategy.

question: Which of the following is a founding member of OPEC?
explanation: Venezuela is a founding member of OPEC. Other founding members are Iran, Iraq, Kuwait and Saudi Arabia. The Organization was formed in September 1960.

question: Government by the wealthy is known as _________
explanation: Plutocracy is a system of government where power is concentrated in the hands of the wealthy. In this system, economic power translates directly into political power, meaning that only the rich influence governance and decision-making.

question: The absence of the rule of law in government will bring about …
explanation: The absence of the rule of law in government will bring about human rights abuse. This is so as the rule of law refers to the constitutional provision which emphasizes the supremacy of the law, the equality before the law and existence of fundamental human rights.

question: The Barclay's Bank and the British Petroleum Company in Nigeria were nationalized in the late 1970s for transacting business with …
explanation: The nationalization of the British Petroleum company meant the loss of considerable revenue to Britain. In addition, the nationalization in 1978 of the British owned Barclays Bank for operating in South- Africa meant that the Barclay Bank no longer profited from handling the transactions of all the public agencies and corporations in Nigeria.

question: In the legislative process, a bill is a ....
explanation: A bill is proposed legislation under consideration by a legislature. Once a bill has been enacted into law, it is called an act of the legislature, or a statute. Bills are introduced in the legislature and are discussed, debated and voted upon.

question: The type of government operated in Nigeria between October 1st 1979 to December 3 1983 is called a __________
explanation: During this period, Nigeria operated under the Second Republic, which was modelled after the United States' presidential system. In this system, the President is both the head of state and the head of government, separate from the legislature. This period marked a shift from the parliamentary system used during the First Republic.

question: The two military coups that toppled civilian regimes in Nigeria were those of ......
explanation: The Civilian government of Alhaji Abubakar Tafawa Balewa was ousted in a bloody coup led by major Chukwuma Nzeogwu in January 15, 1966. This first Military Coup in Nigeria then brought in Major General J.T.U Aguiyi Ironsi as the first Military Head of State of Nigeria On December, 31,1983, the civilian government of Shehu Shagari was overthrown by General Muhammed Buhari and Tunde Idiagbon when they were at Mecca..

question: The highest grade in the Civil Service is known as the ............
explanation: The Administrative cadre comprises the most senior civil servants who organize and coordinate the activities of the ministries. They execute high-level administrative work, advise ministers in the formulation and implementation of policies and serve as the communication link between the minister and other civil servants. Recruitment to this class is based on university education and very competitive written examinations and interviews conducted by the civil service commission. In this class are directors-general, other directors, deputy directors, assistant directors, etc.

question: The main function of the Code of Conduct Bureau is to......

options.text: Give the police more powers to make arrests.
Give the judiciary more powers to discipline erring judges.
Protect public officers from the press

explanation: The Code of Conduct Bureau (CCB) is a Nigerian government agency responsible for promoting accountability, transparency, and ethical behavior among public officials. Its main role is to ensure that public officers do not engage in corrupt practices, abuse of power, or conflicts of interest.

question: Under the 1999 constitution of Nigeria, the power to create local governments is vested in the .....
explanation: Under the 1999 Constitution of Nigeria, the power to create local governments is vested in the state assembly.

question: A major issue that distinguishes pressure groups from political parties is the …
explanation: Political parties aim at contesting and winning elections and controlling government while pressure groups aim at pursuing the interest of their members and influencing the decisions of the government.

question: ____was the first Nigerian Permanent Representative to the United Nations.
explanation: The first Nigerian Permanent Representative to United Nations was General Joseph Garba.

question: The independent National Electoral Commission has the power to prepare and maintain the register of.____
explanation: This is the only body saddled with the responsibility of effecting a credible election by ensuring voter's registration are updated.

question: ________refers to the manipulation of boundaries of constituencies in order to win more seats,
explanation: In representative democracies, Gerrymandering refers to political manipulation of electoral district boundaries with the intent of creating undue advantage for a party, group, or socio-economic class within the constituency

question: The major problem of the ECOWAS is lack of _______
explanation: The major problem of the ECOWAS is lack of common currency. This makes financial transactions difficult among member nations.

question: Before Nigeria became a republic, the highest body charged with the administration of justice was the......
explanation: Before Nigeria became a republic in 1963, the highest court of appeal for the country was the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council (JCPC) in London, United Kingdom. This meant that cases could be appealed from Nigerian courts to the Privy Council, which had the final say on legal matters.

question: After 1945, the demand of African nationalists changed from reform to independence because .....

options.text: The Second World War enhanced colonial rule
The Second World War boosted their morale

explanation: After 1945, the demand of African nationalists changed from reform to independence because the second world war boosted their morale. The war exposed the myth surrounding white supremacy.

question: Who re-organised the Nigeria's four regions into twelve states in May 1967?
explanation: On May 27, 1967, General Yakubu Gowon, who was Nigeria’s Head of State at the time, announced the creation of twelve states from the existing four regions (Northern, Western, Eastern, and Mid-Western regions). This was done to reduce ethnic tensions and prevent the secession of the Eastern Region (which later declared itself the Republic of Biafra, leading to the Nigerian Civil War).

question: Some pre-colonial Nigerian societies are described as stateless because ......

options.text: They had no formal governmental institutions
They had no definite political boundaries

explanation: Some pre-colonial Nigerian societies are described as stateless because they had no formal governmental institutions.

question: The Nigeria's head of government in 1963 was _____
explanation: The head of government was also the prime minister in the person of Abubakar Tafawa Balewa.

question: The lbadan Conference of 1950 was convened to discuss the provisions of the ....
explanation: The Ibadan Conference of 1950 was convened to discuss the provisions of the Macpherson Constitution. Sir John Macphereson became Government of Nigeria in 1948. He then took immediate steps to review Sir Arthur Richard's Constitution of 1946 and fashioned a new constitution which came into being in 1951.

question: A common feature of government is________

Considering that democracy is a government of the people, by the people and for the people, it is imperative that every person within this system is treated equally and fairly. This equality is assured when the rule of law is practiced (the rule that states that no body is above the law/ every one is equal before the law).

explanation: A federal system is a system whereby power is shared among the federal level and the component units. The component units (the states) report to a common authority at the centre (the federal level).

question: Aggregate view of individuals in a society is referred to as
explanation: Public opinion is the beliefs, values and attitudes, which are commonly held and expressed by the majority of the people on a given public issue.

question: The power of prerogative of mercy rests with the
explanation: The "prerogative of mercy" is one of the powers of the executive. It is also a method of checking the activities of the Judiciary. It is the power of the president to grant pardon to a convicted criminal or to commute his/her sentence.

question: The fundamental objective guiding a nation's foreign policy is
explanation: Foreign policy refers to the decisions and actions taken by a state to pursue its interests within the global system. This means that foreign policy is based, fundamentally, on the country's own (national) interest. It can also be based on other country's interest only if they align with the country's own interest.

question: The Nigerian Civil War was fought during the military regime of
explanation: The Nigerian Civil War took place between 1967-70 under the regime of General Yakubu Gowon (1966-75). It was a war between Eastern Nigeria (Biafra) and Nigeria.

question: The Commission that examines complaints of civil wrongs committed by government employees is
explanation: The Public Complaints Commission is a body responsible for receiving an responding to complaints from the public about the wrongdoings of civil servants and other government employees. They have the power to offer recommendations for the punishments of such employees.

question: Nigerian Ports Authority is an example of
explanation: The Nigerian Port Authority is an example of a public corporation. A public corporation is a government organisation that provides essential services to the public. The Nigerian Ports Authority is responsible for providing smooth unloading and offloading of exported and imported cargo.

question: The principle of civil service that guarantees the employment of public workers is
explanation: Permanence is a principle of the civil service that ensures job security for public workers. Once employed, civil servants are guaranteed long-term employment, as long as they adhere to the rules and regulations.

question: Pressure groups are different from political parties because they
explanation: Pressure groups are different from political parties in the sense that while political parties analyse and contest elections and aggregate interests (i.e. bring together people who have differing interests together), pressure groups articulate the interest of people how share a common goal.

question: The most effective instrument adopted by Nigeria against the East-West Cold War in the 1960s was
explanation: During the 1960s, Nigeria adopted the non-alignment policy as an effective instrument to navigate the East-West Cold War. This policy meant that Nigeria chose not to align with either the capitalist bloc (led by the United States) or the communist bloc (led by the Soviet Union). Instead, it focused on maintaining independence in foreign relations and avoiding entanglement in ideological conflicts between the two superpowers.

question: Which of these colonial constitutions in Nigeria endured for the longest period?
explanation: The Clifford Constitution is the colonial constitution that lasted for the longest period (1922-46). The Richards Constitution was adopted in 1946. The Macpherson Constitution was adopted in 1951 while the Lyttleton Constitution was adopted in 1954.

question: The judgement that ceded and transferred Bakassi legal title from Nigeria to Cameroon was delivered by

explanation: The judgement that ceded and transferred the Bakassi Peninsula's legal title from Nigeria to Camerron was delivered by the International Court of Justice (ICJ). The case, titled Land and Maritime Boundary between Cameroon and Nigeria, resolved the long-standing boundary dispute between the two countries.

question: Formation of political parties in Nigeria is one of the features of
explanation: The Clifford Constitution of 1922 is the constitution that officially granted Nigerians the right to create political parties and form political associations, The first political party formed in Nigeria was the Nigerian National Democratic Party (NNDP) formed by Herbert Macauley in 1923.

question: Lack of separation of power is a feature of
explanation: Separation of power is the division of powers and functions among the three arms of government - the legislature, executive and judiciary. This is essential to prevent the abuse of power when it is concentrated in the hands of a single authority. In a presidential system, there is a clear separation of power. In a cabinet system, there is still separation of power although, it is not as clear (this is because the legislature and executive arms are fused). However, in a military government, power is concentrated in the hands of the military leader. He has the power to make laws through the promulgation of decrees; to execute the law; as well as to punish law breakers. In this case, there is a lack of separation of power.

question: Military intervention in Nigerian politics was first witnessed in
explanation: Military intervention was first witnessed on the 25th of January, 1966 when General Aguiyi Ironsi took power from the then Prime Minister, Alhaji Tafawa Balewa. He immediately suspended the constitution and established a unitary system of government. The military claimed that the reason for its intervention was to quell the ethnic tension in the country as well as stop corruption.

question: Under the Hausa pre-colonial administration, the office of the Prime Minister is usually occupied by
explanation: The waziri, in the Hausa pre-colonial era, was the Prime Minister in charge of all the officials in the palace.

question: A naturalised citizen can lose his citizenship if found guilty of
explanation: Treason is the crime of betraying one's own country. A naturalised citizen found guilty of treason will lose his/ her citizenship.

question: The productivity of public corporations is believed to be enhanced when there is
explanation: Public Corporation operates better when there is little to no political interference. This is because it allows the corporation to function like a business rather than a government body, reduce corruption and improve accountability. Measures such as privatisation, commercialisation and deregulation can be taken to reduce political interference

question: The Nigerian Youth Movement pursued its objectives through the use of
explanation: The Nigerian Youth Movement, like most early political parties, pursued its objectives through the use of newspapers. They established their ideologies and aired their opinions concerning political issues through newspapers.

question: Delegated legislation can be regulated through
explanation: Delegated legislation, or secondary legislation, is a law that is made by a governmental body other than the legislature. The legislation often delegates legislative powers to other government bodies such as the local government, public corporations, etc. to create laws that are specific to their jurisdiction. This is because the legislature may not have the necessary expertise to create laws for specific regions or agencies. Though these non-legislative bodies are given the power to make laws, these laws are regulated by the legislature to ensure that they do not lead to abuse of power and that they abide by the legislative standards in the country.

question: Lawyers recruited into the civil service belong to the
explanation: Lawyers belong to the professional class because they provide certain expertise to the civil service (in this case, the provision of legal counsel). Other members of the professional class includes: doctors, engineers, accountants, etc.

explanation: The madawaki was the commander of the army in Pre-colonial Hausa/ Fulani Empire.

explanation: The Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) is a forum of 120 countries that are not formally aligned with or against any major power bloc. It was founded with the view of advancing interests of developing countries in the context of Cold War confrontation.

question: Absence of a Red-tape is a merit of
explanation: Red-tape refers to time-consuming regulations or bureaucratic procedures. The absence of red-tape is one of the merits of a unitary structure. WIthout the several levels that accompanies a federal structure (central, state and local) or a confederal state (central and autonomous unit), decisions are made faster without the need for processing and approval from a higher level.
